pr_title: [Fix #1032] Better/faster performance when querying certificates on OS X
pr_body:
X509 parsing is now handled by OpenSSL as there does seem to be a
memory leak in SecCertificateCopyValues of Security framework which resulted
performance hit when querying certificates. This fixes #1032.

Quick and dirty benchmark:

``` bash
❯ time ./build/darwin/osquery/run --query "select * from certificates" --iterations 10
0.60s user
0.08s system 
87% cpu 
0.785 total
```

And here's the same run on master build:

``` bash
❯ time ./build/darwin/osquery/run --query "select * from certificates" --iterations 10
7.30s user
0.10s system 
98% cpu 
7.534 total
```

`key_usage` and `key_algorithm` columns now display human readable strings
(e.g. Digital Signature, CRL Sign rsaEncryption) than the raw flags and OIDs (e.g 0x86, 1.2.840.1).

Here's how it looks:

```

   key_algorithm = rsaEncryption
       key_usage = Digital Signature, Key Cert Sign, CRL Sign


     common_name = Charles Proxy Custom Root Certificate
              ca = 1
not_valid_before = 946684800
 not_valid_after = 2349272255
   key_algorithm = rsaEncryption
       key_usage = Key Cert Sign
  subject_key_id = 50c52641d8ea1b0f18e00e9e74224b953fb9605d
authority_key_id =
            sha1 = 2eb6f51492b2ce4461590fe5cc0344550837d67c
            path = /Users/sbs/Library/Keychains/login.keychain
```

And no complaints from the profiler:

```
❯ sudo python ./tools/profile.py --leaks --rounds 10 --query "select * from certificates;"
Analyzing leaks in query: select * from certificates;
  definitely: 0 leaks for 0 total leaked bytes.
```

Also, if you want to squash deprecated warnings for the OS-provided OpenSSL you can wrap the API calls with [`OSQUERY_USE_DEPRECATED`](https://github.com/facebook/osquery/blob/master/include/osquery/tables.h#L27). We can also start using the Homebrew-provided OpenSSL and statically link in the symbols we need from libcrypto. It's a cardinal sin on other platforms, but we're already damned on OS X.
I would wrap OpenSSL API calls with `OSQUERY_USE_DEPRECATED` if there were only a handful of them, but there are about ~12-15 calls, which I don't think makes it worth it. But I don't feel strongly about it either way, your call.

I'd guess those link errors stem from using the Homebrew-provided OpenSSL's include headers but the Apple-provided libcrypto.so library for linking.

If it was using the Homebrew-OpenSSL's headers you'll have >TLS1.0 support and thus enable those ASIO/SSL features as well as remove the deprecated warnings which come from header macros.

To completely switch to Homebrew's version we'd have to modify the [provision scripts slightly](https://github.com/facebook/osquery/blob/master/tools/provision/darwin.sh#L29) to add openssl, [assure](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew/blob/master/Library/Formula/openssl.rb#L32) a static version of libcrypto(.a) was installed, and change [CMake's preference](https://github.com/facebook/osquery/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt#L273) for static/dynamic. It's a bit of work, but definitely worth it. 
Yes, you are right, I used Homebrew-provided OpenSSL headers, but linked with Apple's libcrypto.so.
I had already spent way too much time figuring out OpenSSL APIs for relatively simple things and so just stuck with Apple provided OpenSSL.

Thanks for the pointers, those should be very helpful. I will try taking a crack at it later today/tomorrow and will probably still need to ping you on IRC.

This is ready to merge as soon as we figure out how to handle the CA checking. Either we count any non-0 returns from `X509_check_ca` as true or emit the exact return integer. Your call!
Okay, updated so that `X509_check_ca`'s return code  > 0  is true.

issue_context.title: Querying certificates on OS X seems fairly slow
issue_context.body:
Consistently takes over 1 seconds to fetch my local certificates:

```
~ $ time osqueryi "select count(*) from certificates"
+----------+
| count(*) |
+----------+
| 425      |
+----------+
        1.28 real         1.19 user         0.03 sys
~ $ time osqueryi "select count(*) from certificates"
+----------+
| count(*) |
+----------+
| 425      |
+----------+
        1.26 real         1.18 user         0.03 sys
~ $ time osqueryi "select count(*) from certificates"
+----------+
| count(*) |
+----------+
| 425      |
+----------+
        1.44 real         1.25 user         0.05 sys
```

For comparison querying `processes`, `listening_ports`, and `homebrew_packages` all take under 50 milliseconds.
